paragraphs.text: Chapter Six: A Familiar Den of Scum
Tatooine. Three months after the Battle of Endor.
Hahn Solo had never particularly liked Tat-oo-een.
It was hot, dusty, lawless, and populated by an extraordinary number of people who either wanted to kill him or collect money from him.
Unfortunately, it was also one of the few places in the galaxy where he felt entirely at home.
"Coming up on Moss Eyes-lee," he announced.
Chewbacca growled from the copilot's seat.
"Of course I remember what happened last time."
The Wookiee barked something considerably louder.
"All right, maybe some of it was my fault."
The Millennium Falcon descended through the planet's upper atmosphere, its battered hull shuddering as the desert winds caught it.
Below them stretched an endless expanse of orange sand.
Two suns hung low over the horizon.
Hahn glanced toward the passenger seat.
He could almost imagine Luke sitting there, barely more than a kid, staring out at the landscape he had been so desperate to escape.
That had been only four years ago.
Back then, Hahn had been concerned primarily with paying off Jabba the Hutt, keeping the Falcon operational, and avoiding Imperial patrols.
Now Jabba was dead, the Emperor was dead, and Hahn Solo was a celebrated general of the Rebel Alliance.
He still owed money to several people on Tat-oo-een.
Some things, apparently, were beyond the reach of galactic revolution.
The cantina was almost exactly as he remembered it.
Music drifting from the far end of the room.
And the unmistakable smell of cheap liquor, overheated machinery, and several species whose personal hygiene practices Hahn had never understood.
He stepped through the entrance with Chewbacca close behind.
A blue-skinned Duros at the nearest table rose so quickly that his chair fell backward.
A Rodian near the bar muttered something to his companion.
"No," Hahn said. "That was a team effort."
By the time they reached the bar, half the cantina was watching them.
He had spent years trying to remain unnoticed in places like this.
Now complete strangers wanted to buy him drinks.
The bartender, Wuher, stared at him from behind a row of battered containers.
"Thought you'd left the planet for good."
"Then you probably know where the basement is."
"Listen to me, Solo. There are some parts of this place you don't want to go poking around in."
"Funny. That's exactly what people used to say about the Death Star."
Ten minutes later, Hahn and Chewbacca stood in a narrow storage room behind the bar.
Wuher had reluctantly unlocked the door after Chewbacca explained, at considerable volume, that they were acting on behalf of the new galactic government.
Hahn had then explained that Chewbacca's suggestion to remove the door entirely was not strictly necessary.
The storage room contained crates, cleaning equipment, and a refrigerator that sounded as though it had been repaired by someone with a personal dislike of refrigeration.
At the back stood a metal panel.
"Yeah. Brand-new lock on a twenty-year-old door."
Not the cheap equipment usually found in Moss Eyes-lee.
"Somebody really didn't want customers wandering down here."
Chewbacca produced a small tool from his belt.
"You're not going to cut through the door?"
Chewbacca inserted the tool into the access panel.
"Technically, that counts as cutting through the door."
The tunnel beyond was surprisingly clean.
No evidence of the desert settlement above.
A row of recessed lights illuminated the floor.
After several turns, it opened into a circular chamber lined with communications equipment.
Most of the instruments were old.
Some appeared to date back to the Clone Wars.
But several had been replaced recently.
Chewbacca examined a console and growled.
"Yeah," Hahn said. "Somebody's been keeping this place running."
At the center of the room stood a recording terminal.
A list of dates filled the screen.
"The Emperor was listening to this dump."
"Yeah, I know. Apparently he had nothing better to do."
A group of smugglers argued over shipping tariffs.
Two Imperial officers discussed a missing shipment of weapons.
A frightened merchant offered a bribe to a customs inspector.
"Half the people in this place were breaking the law."
Chewbacca gave him a long look.
Then a familiar name caught his eye.
Wearing the same vest he still owned.
Beneath the photograph was a short assessment.
Independent freighter captain. Questionable reliability. Significant financial liabilities. Likely to encounter fatal difficulties within one standard year.
Hahn stared at the final sentence.
Chewbacca laughed so hard he had to grip the console.
The day he had met Luke Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi.
The hologram showed his younger self seated at a table with the old Jedi and a nervous farm boy.
Hahn felt an unexpected pang of nostalgia.
He had almost forgotten how the man looked.
The infuriating calm with which he had discussed impossible things.
A good man, Hahn now understood.
A man who had given his life to help them escape.
A burst of static filled the room.
Hahn's own voice, younger and more arrogant.
Old Ben discussed transportation to Alderaan.
Luke sat beside him, looking as though he had never been inside a room containing so many dangerous people.
A small red symbol flashed beside Obi-Wan's image.
Voice and facial characteristics consistent with General Obi-Wan Kenobi.
Identification added following the Battle of Yavin.
"So they didn't know who he was at the time."
"Yeah. Somebody went through these recordings afterward."
The identification had been added weeks after Luke destroyed the first Death Star.
Pal-puh-teen's agents had been searching backward through old surveillance records, trying to understand how the boy from Tat-oo-een had reached the Rebellion.
The Emperor had been dead for three months.
But his intelligence machinery had spent decades collecting fragments of people's lives.
Fragments that could be assembled long after the people themselves had forgotten the conversations.
The next discovery was less amusing.
A collection of transport records occupied a separate section of the archive.
Most concerned ordinary Imperial cargo shipments.
But several had been marked with a designation Hahn recognized from Lay-uh's briefing.
A shipment had arrived on Tat-oo-een several years before Alderaan's destruction.
And a series of memory-storage components whose purpose Hahn did not understand.
The receiving authority was listed as an Imperial research office.
No location beyond the cantina's underground station.
This one contained a voice recording.
A man spoke in formal, precise Basic.
"Transfer authorization confirmed. Aurel Seven subjects are to remain isolated from all civilian traffic. No correspondence. No unauthorized visitors."
"Does that sound like somebody we know?"
The voice sounded like the captain who had welcomed Lay-uh to the Imperial Palace.
But the recording was years old.
Original sample acquired: Imperial year fourteen.
"Looks like it isn't necessarily the real guy talking."
Even the slight roughness in the final syllables.
He understood why Lay-uh had been so disturbed by the interrogation recording.
Someone had built a machine capable of making a person appear to say things they had never said.
And that machine had been operating for years.
He copied the files onto a portable data cylinder.
"Lay-uh's going to want to see this."
The same day the Emperor's private chamber on Kor-uh-sant had been accessed.
The file had been opened remotely.
The authorization belonged to one of Pal-puh-teen's advisers.
That name had appeared in the Emperor's personal records.
One of the strange men who had accompanied him to the second Death Star.
Yet someone was still using his credentials.
Only one file had been retrieved.
Time of delivery: the morning Darren had jumped.
Hahn felt a cold sensation settle in his stomach.
"I think we just found out what set Darren off."
A sharp metallic click sounded behind them.
At the entrance stood a security droid.
Its single red optical sensor moved between them.
"Yeah, well, we're kind of authorized now."
The blaster bolt struck its shoulder, spinning it sideways.
A red bolt struck the ceiling.
Chewbacca seized the droid by one arm and slammed it against the wall.
Its weapon clattered across the floor.
The machine attempted to strike him with its remaining arm.
Hahn emerged from behind the console.
The droid's head separated from its body.
It bounced twice and rolled across the floor.
Chewbacca stood over the wreckage, breathing heavily.
Hahn looked at the destroyed machine.
Somewhere deeper in the facility, machinery began moving.
A warning light illuminated above the door.
"Does every Imperial secret room do that?"
They emerged into the cantina storage room just as the underground security shutters slammed shut behind them.
Wuher stared at the smoking access panel.
"I told you not to go down there!"
"Yeah, well, you forgot to mention the killer droids."
Back aboard the Falcon, Hahn transmitted the recovered records to Lay-uh through an encrypted Alliance channel.
He waited while the connection established.
Her hologram appeared above the console.
"Found your secret station. Found some recordings. Nearly got killed by a security droid."
A satisfied growl came from the copilot's seat.
"Listen, sweetheart. We found something about Darren."
"Someone sent an activation command from this station to Kor-uh-sant on the morning he jumped."
"That's the interesting part. The authorization belonged to Sim Ah-loo."
"But he died aboard the second Death Star."
"There's something else. The station was recording people for years. Voices, conversations, all kinds of things. Somebody's been using those recordings to manufacture commands."
"Not yet. Most of the records are encrypted."
"Hahn, I want you to bring those files back."
"We can send a proper intelligence team later. Those records may explain what happened to Darren."
"Don't thank me yet. I haven't sent you the bill."
For a moment, he stared at the data cylinder resting beside the controls.
An entire secret Imperial operation beneath a cantina.
Recordings of conversations from years ago.
Someone using the voice of a dead Emperor's adviser to activate a command inside another man's mind.
"Yeah. Smuggling spice. Dodging customs. Running away from people who wanted to kill us."
Outside, the twin suns were sinking toward the horizon.
The Falcon lifted from the landing bay and climbed into the orange sky.
It came from an unknown transmitter somewhere in Moss Eyes-lee.
The screen displayed a single sentence.
GENERAL SOLO. THE EMPEROR IS DEAD. HIS ORDERS ARE NOT.
YOU HAVE TAKEN SOMETHING THAT DOES NOT BELONG TO YOU.
RETURN THE RECORDS, OR THE NEXT VOICE YOU HEAR MAY BE YOUR OWN.
For once, neither of them had anything to say.
